newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CZK 5bln, 5-yr bond ave yield hits 10.57 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech CZK 5bln, 5-yr bond ave yield hits 10.57 pct.

text.p: An auction of a five billion crown ($180.8 million) tranche of Czech five-year state bonds produced an average yield of 10.57 percent, the central bank said on Tuesday.
The central bank said the auction was heavily oversubscribed, with bids totalling 18.5 billion crowns.
The bonds have an annual coupon of 10.55 percent.
The central bank said the maximum yield was 10.6 percent, and the minimum yield was 10.44 percent.
Analysts said the issue attracted many foreign investors due to the implementation of new tax rules for bonds issued from January 1, 1997.
State bonds are now subject to a 25-percent withholding tax for both foreign and domestic investors, which has forced the state to offer higher yields and in turn, attract more foreign investors.
Previously, domestic investors were exempt from the rule, allowing the state to offer lower yields.
